text:
maya: Hey team — noticing our error budget burn for the availability SLO spiking in Grafana for eu-west over the last 40m but there was no user-visible outage. Can we sanity-check how we're computing the SLI and whether ingestion lag is skewing burn rates?

jon: I saw that too. Looks like prometheus remote_write ingestion lag hit ~4m during a kube node upgrade window. If recording rules are evaluated on the ingestion side, dashboards can show a sudden blow-up.

sam: Agreed. Two quick suspects: 1) queries using raw request counters instead of recording rules, 2) alerts using instant() vs rate() and getting noisy on scrape gaps.

maya: Current availability SLI query in the dashboard is this (raw):
```
sum(inference_success_total{region="eu-west"}) / sum(inference_request_total{region="eu-west"})
```
We surface that as a percentage and feed into the burn panel.

liam: That's the issue — raw counters evaluated during ingestion lag can drop to zero or flatline and create transient 100% error rates. We should have a recording rule that normalizes with increase() over a window and a force-fill for missing data.

jon: Proposal: switch to a recording rule like:
```
- record: slo:availability:ratio:30m
  expr: sum(increase(inference_success_total[30m])) / sum(increase(inference_request_total[30m]))
```
Then use that recorded metric in Grafana panels and the error budget calc. Avoid instant() queries.

sam: Also add an ingestion-lag panel (prometheus_ts_seconds - local_ts_seconds) for each remote_write instance and add it to the SLO dashboard. If lag > 120s, gray out burn computations or annotate the graph.

maya: For alerting: currently we fire errorbudget-burn > 10%/hr which hit during that window. Suggest we add a guard: only count burn when ingestion_lag < 120s for the region; otherwise alert a separate issue (ingestion-lag-high).

liam: I'm fine with that. We should also stop mixing region-level SLOs with global error budget math. If eu-west has its own SLO, its burn shouldn't move global budget unless > X%.

jon: On saturation SLI: GPU utilization > 90% should be measured with a 5m rolling average and we should use node-level allocatable_gpus as denominator (avoid host-level GPUs that are offline). Recording rule example:
```
- record: slo:gpu_saturation:5m
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent[5m])
```
Then create a saturation-to-burn mapping: sustained >90% for 15m == burn rate Y.

sam: Action items I can take: 1) PR adding the two recording rules (availability:30m and gpu_saturation:5m) to infra/observability, 2) Grafana panel for ingestion-lag + annotation logic, 3) modify alert rules to gate on ingestion_lag. Will open PR and link here.

maya: Thanks. Also let's define SLO window explicitly in the doc: 30d rolling, with the availability SLI computed from the 30m ratio recording rule. Add a note to exclude maintenance windows shorter than 10m if planned and annotated.

liam: One more: export format for error budget reporting (finance/ops) needs a CSV with columns: region, window_start, window_end, error_budget_remaining_percent, burn_rate_per_hour. We should add a Grafana report panel or an API endpoint to dump that.

jon: I'll add a short runbook for on-call: if errorbudget alert fires but ingestion_lag > 120s, mark as "observability issue" and escalate to infra-obs. If ingestion_lag < 120s and burn persists, follow SLO mitigation playbook (scale dedicated pool, trigger fallback model).

infra-bot: alert: prometheus-remote-write:ingestion-lag(eu-west) exceeded 240s on rw-instance-3 at 1789123600 — auto-ticket #OBS-412 created.

maya: ok thanks all — sam, please paste PR link here and we'll try to merge before next oncall handover.

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2312 — adds recording rules + dashboard panels + alert gating. PTAL.

jon: LGTM, will validate on staging once merged.

liam: I'll follow up to add the CSV export prototype to the reporting job.

maya: Closing loop — once merged, update the SLO doc and notify finance + platform teams. :thumbsup:
